meaning: if; when; once (X happens, then Y)
notes: The most flexible conditional. Y happens after X is complete, so it also means 'when/once'. It can also describe a one-time discovery in the past: 家に帰ったら、手紙が来ていた (When I got home, a letter had come).
match: (?<=[っんいしちりきぎびみえけせてねべめれ])(たら|だら)(?![けし？?]|どう|いかが|いい|よい|なあ|な。)
examples: 雨が降っ{たら}、試合は中止です。
If it rains, the match will be called off.
駅に着い{たら}、電話してください。
Please call me once you arrive at the station.
安かっ{たら}、買います。
If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

meaning: if (condition → result)
formation: る-verb: 食べる → 食べれば
う-verb: e-row + ば (行く → 行けば, 読む → 読めば)
い-adj: 〜ければ (安い → 安ければ)
な-adj / Noun: 〜なら(ば) / 〜であれば
notes: Focuses on the condition itself: if X is true, Y follows. Common in advice and general truths. The result is usually not a command or request when the subject of both clauses is the same.
match: (?<=[えけげせてねべめれ])(ば)(?!なら|いけ|いい|よい|よかっ|かり)
examples: この薬を飲め{ば}、すぐ治りますよ。
If you take this medicine, you'll get better soon.
時間があれ{ば}、手伝います。
If I have time, I'll help.
安けれ{ば}、二つ買いたいです。
If it's cheap, I'd like to buy two.

meaning: when; whenever; if (X, then Y always/naturally follows)
notes: Used for natural or automatic results, habits, directions and machines: this button → that happens. Y cannot be a request, wish or intention.
examples: 春になる{と}、桜が咲きます。
When spring comes, the cherry blossoms bloom.
このボタンを押す{と}、ドアが開きます。
When you press this button, the door opens.
まっすぐ行く{と}、右に駅があります。
If you go straight, the station is on the right.

meaning: if (it's the case that); if you're talking about
formation: Verb / い-adj plain form + なら
notes: Picks up a situation (often something the other person said) and gives advice or an opinion about it: 'If you're going to Kyoto, ...'. Unlike たら, Y can happen before X: 京都に行くなら、この本を読んでおくといい.
examples: 京都に行く{なら}、秋がいいですよ。
If you're going to Kyoto, autumn is a good time.
日本料理{なら}、寿司が一番好きです。
When it comes to Japanese food, I like sushi best.
疲れている{なら}、早く寝たほうがいい。
If you're tired, you should go to bed early.

meaning: even if; even though; no matter (how/what...)
notes: Y happens regardless of X. With question words it means 'no matter...': いくら食べても太らない (No matter how much I eat, I don't gain weight).
match: (?:(?<=[っいしきぎりびみちえけせねべめれく])(?<!なく)(ても)|(?<=ん)(でも))(?![のうしい、よ良]|かまわ|構わ)
examples: 雨が降っ{ても}、行きます。
Even if it rains, I'll go.
いくら練習し{ても}、上手になりません。
No matter how much I practise, I don't get better.
高く{ても}、この時計が欲しいです。
Even if it's expensive, I want this watch.

meaning: may; it's OK to (permission)
formation: Also: 〜てもかまわない (it's fine if...)
notes: Asks for or gives permission. 〜てもかまいません is a little more formal and sounds like 'I don't mind if...'.
match: (?<!なく)([てで]も(?:いい|よい|良い|かまわ|構わ))
examples: ここで写真を撮っ{てもいい}ですか。
May I take photos here?
もう帰っ{てもいい}ですよ。
You can go home now.
窓を開け{てもかまいません}か。
Do you mind if I open the window?

meaning: must not; not allowed to
formation: Verb て-form + はいけない
Casual: 〜ちゃだめ / 〜ちゃいけない
notes: Prohibition. Teachers, parents and rules use it; to a superior it sounds strong, so 〜ないでください is softer.
examples: ここでたばこを吸っ{てはいけません}。
You must not smoke here.
試験中に話し{てはいけない}。
You are not allowed to talk during the exam.
この川で泳い{ではいけません}。
You must not swim in this river.

meaning: must; have to
formation: Verb ない-stem + なければならない / なければいけない
Also: 〜なくてはいけない / 〜ないといけない
notes: Literally 'if (I) don't, it won't do'. ならない is more about rules and duty, いけない about personal need. In speech the second half is often dropped: もう行かなきゃ (I've got to go).
match: (なければ(?:なら|いけ)|なくては(?:なら|いけ)|ないと(?:いけ|だめ))
examples: 明日までにレポートを出さ{なければなりません}。
I have to hand in the report by tomorrow.
毎日薬を飲ま{なくてはいけない}。
I must take medicine every day.
もう帰ら{ないといけない}。
I have to go home now.

meaning: don't have to; it's not necessary to
formation: Verb ない-stem + なくてもいい
Formal: 〜なくてもかまいません
notes: The opposite of 〜なければならない: there is no obligation.
match: (なくても(?:いい|よい|良い|かまわ|構わ))
examples: 明日は来{なくてもいい}ですよ。
You don't have to come tomorrow.
全部食べ{なくてもいい}です。
You don't have to eat all of it.
急が{なくてもかまいません}。
There's no need to hurry.

meaning: to do completely; to do by accident or with regret
notes: Two nuances: finishing something completely (宿題をしてしまった), or something regrettable or unintended (財布をなくしてしまった). In speech it shortens to 〜ちゃう: 食べちゃった.
match: ([てで]しま(?:った|いました|います|う))
examples: 財布をなくし{てしまいました}。
I (unfortunately) lost my wallet.
ケーキを全部食べ{てしまった}。
I ate the whole cake.
電車の中で寝{てしまった}。
I fell asleep on the train.

meaning: to do in advance; to leave something as it is
formation: Casual: 〜とく / 〜どく (やっとく, 読んどく)
notes: Doing something now in preparation for later, or leaving something in a state on purpose: 窓を開けておいてください (Please leave the window open).
examples: 旅行の前にホテルを予約し{ておきます}。
I'll book the hotel before the trip.
パーティーの飲み物を買っ{ておいた}。
I bought drinks for the party in advance.
使ったら、元の場所に戻し{ておいて}ください。
After using it, please put it back where it was.

meaning: has been done (and the result remains)
formation: Object usually takes が: 窓が開けてある
notes: Describes a state left by someone's deliberate action, without saying who did it. Compare 窓が開いている (the window is open) with 窓が開けてある (the window has been opened, on purpose).
match: (?<=[っいしきぎりえけせねべめれ])(てあ(?:る|り|っ))
examples: 壁にカレンダーが貼っ{てあります}。
A calendar has been put up on the wall.
テーブルに花が飾っ{てある}。
Flowers have been arranged on the table.
ノートに名前が書い{てあります}。
A name is written in the notebook.

meaning: to try doing (to see what it's like)
notes: Trying something out of curiosity, not 'attempting something hard' (that is 〜ようとする).
match: ([てで]み(?:る|た|ます|まし|よう|て|ない|れ)(?!な))
examples: 日本語で手紙を書い{てみました}。
I tried writing a letter in Japanese.
一度日本に行っ{てみたい}です。
I'd like to go to Japan once.
新しいラーメン屋に行っ{てみました}。
I tried the new ramen shop.

meaning: change continuing into the future / change up to now; go and do / come having done
notes: With change verbs, 〜ていく points from now into the future and 〜てくる from the past up to now: 寒くなってきた (It has started getting cold). With movement they mean doing something on the way: 傘を持っていく (take an umbrella).
examples: だんだん寒くなっ{てきました}。
It's gradually got colder.
これから人口は減っ{ていく}でしょう。
The population will probably keep falling from now on.
雨が降りそうだから、傘を持っ{ていって}ください。
It looks like rain, so please take an umbrella.

meaning: to do something for someone (as a favour)
notes: The speaker (or their side) does a favour for someone else. Saying it directly to the person can sound condescending, so 手伝いましょうか is often better than 手伝ってあげます.
match: ([てで](?:あげ|上げ)(?:る|た|ます|まし|よう|て|ない))
examples: 妹に本を読ん{であげました}。
I read a book to my little sister.
友達に駅までの道を教え{てあげた}。
I showed my friend the way to the station.
おばあさんの荷物を持っ{てあげました}。
I carried an elderly woman's bags for her.

meaning: someone does something for me / us
notes: The favour comes toward the speaker's side, and the speaker is grateful. The giver is the subject (marked with が or は).
match: ([てで]くれ(?:る|た|ます|まし|ない|て))
examples: 友達が引っ越しを手伝っ{てくれました}。
My friend helped me move.
母が弁当を作っ{てくれた}。
My mother made me a packed lunch.
ちょっと待っ{てくれません}か。
Could you wait a moment?

meaning: to have someone do something (for me); to get someone to do
notes: The receiver is the subject and the person who does the favour takes に: 友達に手伝ってもらった (I had my friend help me). 〜ていただけませんか is one of the politest requests.
match: ([てで](?:もら|いただ|頂)(?:う|っ|い|え|わ))
examples: 友達に宿題を手伝っ{てもらいました}。
I had my friend help me with my homework.
医者に診{てもらった}ほうがいいですよ。
You should get a doctor to look at it.
もう一度説明し{ていただけません}か。
Could you explain it once more, please?

meaning: I want (someone) to do
formation: Person に + Verb て-form + ほしい
Negative: 〜ないでほしい (I don't want you to...)
notes: Expresses the speaker's wish about someone else's action. Said directly to a superior it can be too strong; use a request instead.
examples: もっとゆっくり話し{てほしい}です。
I'd like you to speak more slowly.
子どもには元気に育っ{てほしい}。
I want my children to grow up healthy.
このことは誰にも言わ{ないでほしい}。
I don't want you to tell anyone about this.

meaning: why don't you...? (suggestion)
formation: Verb た-form + らどうですか
More polite: 〜たらいかがですか
notes: A gentle suggestion. The casual version is just 〜たら？ with rising intonation: 休んだら？
examples: 少し休ん{だらどうですか}。
Why don't you rest a little?
先生に聞い{たらどうですか}。
Why don't you ask the teacher?
こちらの席に座っ{たらいかがですか}。
Would you like to sit in this seat?

meaning: had better; should
formation: Verb た-form + ほうがいい
Verb ない-form + ほうがいい
notes: Advice. The past た-form is usual for the positive (行ったほうがいい), but the negative uses ない (行かないほうがいい).
examples: 熱があるなら、病院に行った{ほうがいい}ですよ。
If you have a fever, you'd better go to the hospital.
夜遅くまでゲームをしない{ほうがいい}。
You shouldn't play games until late at night.
傘を持っていった{ほうがいい}と思います。
I think you should take an umbrella.

meaning: should just; all you have to do is; what should I...?
formation: Question: どうすればいいですか (What should I do?)
notes: Gives (or asks for) the simplest way to get a result. どうすればいいですか is the standard way to ask for advice.
examples: どうすれ{ばいい}ですか。
What should I do?
分からなければ、先生に聞け{ばいい}。
If you don't understand, just ask the teacher.
何時に来れ{ばいい}ですか。
What time should I come?
